says: A relative frame location whose first folder holds " (", a space or a parenthesis before its first separator still keeps part of that folder in the stored frame, because START's relative branch [^\s()]*[/\\] stops at that character and opens falls back to a later " ("; StrayInput's relative root always starts with a fixed prefix and sink-<word>, so S4 never draws it, and two START plants survive the laws.
proof: Running Sink.ts's START, opens, located and portable at 3e6fb58, copied into a scratch script: 'at fn (a (b/private/c.ts:1:2)' gives 'at fn (a (c.ts:1:2)', 'at fn (my (copy)/src/a.ts:1:2)' gives 'at fn (my (a.ts:1:2)', 'at fn (my dir/a (b/c.ts:1:2)' gives 'at fn (my dir/a (c.ts:1:2)', 'at fn (a)b/c (d/e.ts:1:2)' gives 'at fn (a)b/c (e.ts:1:2)', 'at fn (a(b/c (d/e.ts:1:2)' gives 'at fn (a(b/c (e.ts:1:2)'. The f83e0e9e8 cut stores each with no folder. Sink.test.ts:1026 builds the relative root as `${prefix}sink-${word}${separator}${folder}...`, and FrameWord (Sink.test.ts:739) is /^[a-z]{3,16}$/.
cost: A stack with relative locations whose first folder is named with a space or a parenthesis, such as 'my (copy)/', stores part of that folder, against 0186; rare in next/ today, and no stored record of such a stack was read.
